title: Change Annals software and contracts
summary: Modify Annals code, CLI, storage, AI-reader, inbox, installation, or public behavior.
use_when: Annals code, tests, terminology, public CLI, storage, reconciliation, inbox, liaison, installation, or release behavior is being changed.
do_not_use_when: The request is ordinary use or operation of an installed library.
The change belongs to Nucleus shared execution rather than Annals domain behavior.
Publication or deployment has not been separately authorized.
outcome: A minimal, tested Annals change using canonical vocabulary and preserving exact domain, execution, migration, installation, and documentation boundaries.
effects: Modifies Annals source, tests, fixtures, or documentation.
May require coordinated Nucleus contract work when the requester boundary changes.
Release and installation actions remain separate and may mutate Git, installed binaries, database state, scheduler state, or configuration.
authority: Annals owns works, corpus meaning, reconciliation, history, inbox policy, domain recovery, and its installation.
Nucleus owns shared model execution and authentication but never Annals domain success or retry policy.
success: Canonical terminology matches the registered Semantics repository `annals` and affected behavior contracts are updated.
Affected installation, migration, inbox, and live requester canaries are run when the change crosses those boundaries.
failure_and_recovery: Do not infer compatibility from the shared workspace alone; product release, schema, and Nucleus protocol remain separate axes.
Use guarded installed fresh-state or schema migration procedures rather than ad hoc database edits.
Preserve Annals domain results when later Nucleus runtime failure occurs.
privacy: Tests, experiments, source fixtures, libraries, spools, backups, and Nucleus output may contain retained source and model context.
Do not add contributor instructions or Semantics repository output to the constrained liaison runtime prompt.
steps: Read `semantics.repository.explore`, query `semantics repository show annals`, and identify the Annals-owned contract being changed.
If the change crosses Nucleus execution, authentication, compatibility, persistent state, deployment, or requester integration, run `nucleus manual` before design.
Implement the smallest change and update the owning CLI, architecture, data, installation, telemetry, or Semantics terminology authority in the same change.
Run `./annals/ci.sh` and perform separately authorized live canaries when required.
checkpoints: Current technical and plain-language terms follow the registered Semantics repository while code, tests, and component documentation remain behavior authority.
Annals domain state remains authoritative over model prose and Nucleus terminal state.
Migration, rollback, and historical decoding are explicit when persistent meaning changes.
Release or deployment has not occurred without separate authorization.
adaptation: Select only the contract documents relevant to the changed domain while always reading the complete Semantics repository first.
Use the installed Nucleus manual and current Annals installation guide for cross-system or deployment facts that may evolve.
stop_when: A source or corpus semantic cannot be expressed consistently with the canonical model.
A destructive migration or installed fresh-state cutover lacks explicit authority and recovery material.
An affected shared execution change has not been reconciled with Nucleus's owning contract.
does_not_authorize: Running `annals/release.sh`, which commits, tags, and pushes.
Deploying or replacing the installed Annals library.
Changing Nucleus shared policy solely from the requester side.

consumers.statement: A contributor or interactive development agent may use this operation for an authorized Annals code, test, terminology, public contract, storage, inbox, liaison, installation, or release-behavior change.
This operation does not cover ordinary product use, changes owned solely by Nucleus, release publication, or installed deployment without separate authority.

preconditions.statement: The contributor has read the installed Semantics exploration contract and complete current annals repository, identified the owning Annals behavior contract, and has a scoped authorized change.
A change crossing Nucleus execution, authentication, compatibility, persistent state, deployment, or requester integration requires the installed Nucleus manual and owning boundary before design.

inputs.statement: Input is one scoped Annals change request plus the current Semantics terminology, owning product documentation, source, tests, and any separately required installed operational contract.
Historical experiment vocabulary, Semantics repository output as liaison runtime input, and requester-side invention of Nucleus policy are not valid change inputs.

outputs.statement: The result is the smallest coherent source, test, fixture, and owning-documentation change with canonical terminology and a green ./annals/ci.sh gate.
A development result does not itself include Git publication, installed deployment, destructive migration, or a live production success claim.

data_semantics.statement: The registered annals Semantics repository governs maintained contributor terminology, while code, tests, and component documentation remain authoritative for behavior.
Work, source delivery, examination, reconciliation, commit, revision, inbox job, and retry event remain distinct Annals lifecycle concepts.
Nucleus terminal state and model prose remain execution evidence rather than Annals domain success.

identity_and_units.statement: Semantics concept IDs and revisions, Annals provider release and entry contract versions, package versions, library schema, and Nucleus protocol identify separate change and compatibility domains.
This development operation promises no domain measurement, usage, price, or accounting unit.

completeness_and_freshness.statement: The operation begins from the current authoritative Semantics repository and current owning project contracts and updates every affected behavior contract in the same change.
Completion requires the full Annals product gate and any separately authorized boundary-specific migration, installation, inbox, or requester canary that the change affects.
No development duration, universal review coverage, or guarantee about unrelated product areas is promised.

access.statement: The operation uses the current local workspace, filesystem, and shell through an interactive agent session under repository instructions.
Development authority does not grant release, deployment, destructive installed-state replacement, external disclosure, or direct Semantics-state editing.

lifecycle_and_consistency.statement: Select the owning contract, make one minimal coherent change, update corresponding documentation and compatibility or recovery material, then run the complete product gate before handoff.
Persistent meaning changes retain historical decoding and define migration and rollback rather than rewriting old state in place.
Annals domain results survive later Nucleus runtime failure and publication or installation remains a separately authorized lifecycle.

operational_limits.statement: Every code change must leave ./annals/ci.sh green, contributor Semantics output must not enter liaison context, and destructive migration or installed fresh state stops without exact authority and recovery material.
No maximum change size, completion time, or automatic availability of live canaries is promised.

compatibility_and_evolution.statement: Product release, library schema, Nucleus public protocol, immutable tool registrations, installed packaging, provider schema, and entry contract version are evaluated separately.
A public or persistent semantic change updates its owning documentation, migration, rollback, and historical decoder in the same coherent change.
No release cadence, compatibility window, or deprecation period is promised by the development operation.

reliances.statement: Annals development relies on the registered Semantics repository for current maintained terminology while retaining project sources as behavior authority.
A documentation dependency or conditional requirement to consult Nucleus must not be interpreted as unconditional Nucleus runtime authority over an Annals change.
